objective: Decide where Pi-PE fits between Pi Protocol, Pi-Dev, and the software-factory workflow principles, and select the smallest safe integration path.

includes: Current local implementations of pi-protocol, pi-pe, pi-dev, and the SSSF workflow principles
Package ownership, composition boundaries, compatibility blockers, provenance, and first implementation slice
excludes: Installing dependencies or executing package tests
Designing DAG, distributed, or human-approval infrastructure
constraints: Run on pi-coding-agent through Pi Protocol
Keep pipeline definitions data-only and fail closed
Do not duplicate canonical authority or provenance

questions.question: Which package should own each layer of the combined system?
questions.scope: Capability kernel, deterministic pipeline execution, and development workflow semantics

questions.question: What blocks immediate Pi-PE composition of Pi-Dev roles?
questions.scope: Current schema, mapping, receipt, and cancellation implementations

questions.question: What is the smallest safe implementation slice?

claims.statement: Pi Protocol is the capability, authority, session, receipt, and provenance kernel and explicitly is not a workflow engine.
Pi-PE already owns deterministic data-only linear pipeline validation, mapping, bounded execution, dependency pinning, definition persistence, reconciliation, and generated protocol registration.

Pi-PE does not own work-unit lifecycle, development acceptance gates, same-session correction, workspace policy, or durable resumable run state, and its explicit limits make it a poor owner for those domain semantics.

Pi-Dev currently owns independently callable software-development roles and deliberately has no hidden orchestrator, making an explicit discoverable workflow layer a domain extension rather than an implicit behavior change.
Immediate Pi-PE/Pi-Dev composition is blocked by Pi-PE's narrow persisted schema subset because Pi-Dev contracts use canonical keywords such as maxLength and maxItems.

Pi-PE currently extracts the tracked invocation result without retaining canonical receipt metadata, so receipt projection and outcome-unknown behavior require focused integration work before traces can serve as workflow evidence.
The best current option is to keep Pi-PE generic and compose it beneath an explicit Pi-Dev development-workflow layer, without merging the packages or creating a new generic workflow package yet.

evidence_links.note: The package declares its kernel boundary and canonical receipt ownership.

evidence_links.locator: README feature and limitation sections; PipelineSpecV1 and execution detail types
evidence_links.note: The implemented DSL and runtime align with a generic deterministic pipeline layer.
The package explicitly has no retries, rollback, branches, or durable run model beyond returned execution details.
The required development workflow semantics are materially broader than Pi-PE pipeline execution.
Pi-Dev owns roles and explicitly documents the absence of hidden orchestration.
Pi-PE rejects unsupported keys and validates persisted dependencies.
Pi-Dev schemas use maxLength and maxItems, which Pi-PE's subset rejects.
The tracked call is reduced to its result before PipelineExecutor builds step traces.

evidence_links.locator: README package boundary and provenance sections
evidence_links.note: The kernel already owns generic invocation concerns, so a new workflow layer should compose through it.
Pi-PE is already a coherent reusable lower-level engine whose explicit limits should be preserved.
Adding workflows to Pi-Dev could contradict its no-orchestrator intent unless the new layer is explicit, optional, and discoverable.
Development lifecycle semantics belong in code above bounded agent phases, not in the generic capability kernel.

conclusion.summary: Keep Pi-PE as the generic deterministic pipeline engine and compose it beneath an explicit Pi-Dev workflow layer. Fix schema interoperability and receipt preservation first; then ship a read-only scout-adapter-architect plan-change workflow.
conclusion.decision_impact: Avoid a new generic workflow package and avoid merging Pi-PE into Pi-Dev. Sequence implementation around compatibility, provenance, deterministic handoff, pipeline provisioning, and finally development lifecycle semantics.
